text: Mark Twain's The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn was removed from the shelves of Concord's public library a month after its publication, when the committee in charge voted to take it out, fearing that Huck Finn's irreverence would undermine the morals of young readers. In 1885, when the American edition was issued, several libraries banned it from their shelves. The early criticism focused on what was perceived as the book's crudeness.
